session.question: How did the learning curve for DIEP breast reconstruction change over time in this study?
session.answer: The learning curve for DIEP (deep inferior epigastric perforator) flap breast reconstruction improved over time, but the magnitude of improvement differed by level of analysis. At the institutional level, the clearest change was a reduction in hospital stay in the later cases, while most other outcomes remained largely unchanged. At the single-surgeon level, improvement was more pronounced: total operative time decreased for both single- and double-DIEP procedures, flap ischemia time was shorter, and hospital stay was reduced. Importantly, flap loss and overall complication rates did not differ significantly between early and late cases, indicating that technical efficiency improved without an evident tradeoff in safety. (varnava2023breastreconstructionwith chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-2f32301f: This 2023 retrospective study evaluated DIEP flap breast reconstruction learning curves at both the institution level and for a single surgeon, using 115 patients and 161 flaps from July 2018 to June 2021. Cases were divided into early and late groups. At the institutional level, the main improvement over time was a shorter hospital stay in the late group, while most other outcomes did not change significantly. For the single surgeon, performance improved more clearly over time: total surgery time decreased significantly for both single and double DIEP procedures, flap ischemia time was shorter, and hospital stay was reduced. Flap loss and other complications did not significantly differ between early and late cases.
From Charalampos Varnava, Philipp Wiebringhaus, Tobias Hirsch, Alexander Dermietzel, and Maximilian Kueckelhaus. Breast reconstruction with diep flap: the learning curve at a breast reconstruction center and a single-surgeon study. Journal of Clinical Medicine, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/jcm12082894, doi:10.3390/jcm12082894.

At the single-surgeon level, improvement was more pronounced: total operative time decreased for both single- and double-DIEP procedures, flap ischemia time was shorter, and hospital stay was reduced.
